audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel / Shemuel Aleph chapter 30, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Ziklag's burning, captives, collective grief, threatened stoning, ephod inquiry, Besor exhaustion, abandoned Egyptian servant, food and restored strength, negotiated safety, prolonged attack, recovery, spoil terminology, equal-share ruling, and political gift distribution.

verses.restored: When David and his men came to Ziklag on third day, Amalekites had made a raid against Negev and against Ziklag. They struck Ziklag and burned it with fire.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when David and his men were come to Ziklag on the third day, that the Amalekites had invaded the south, and Ziklag, and smitten Ziklag, and burned it with fire;

modern.text: On the third day David and his men arrived in Ziklag, and the Amalekites had raided the Negev, attacked Ziklag, and burned it down.

original.text: וַיְהִ֞י בְּבֹ֨א דָוִ֧ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֛יו צִֽקְלַ֖ג בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י וַעֲמָלֵקִ֣י פָֽשְׁט֗וּ אֶל נֶ֨גֶב֙ וְאֶל צִ֣קְלַ֔ג וַיַּכּוּ֙ אֶת צִ֣קְלַ֔ג וַיִּשְׂרְפ֥וּ אֹתָ֖הּ בָּאֵֽשׁ

verses.restored: They took captive women who were in it, from small to great. They did not put anyone to death, but led them away and went on their way.

familiar.text: And had taken the women captives, that were therein: they slew not any, either great or small, but carried them away, and went on their way.

modern.text: They had taken captive the women and all who were there, both young and old. They had not killed anyone, but had carried them off as they went on their way.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁבּ֨וּ אֶת הַנָּשִׁ֤ים אֲשֶׁר בָּהּ֙ מִקָּטֹ֣ן וְעַד גָּד֔וֹל לֹ֥א הֵמִ֖יתוּ אִ֑ישׁ וַיִּֽנְהֲג֔וּ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ לְדַרְכָּֽם

verses.restored: David and his men came to city, and look, it was burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive.

familiar.text: So David and his men came to the city, and, behold, it was burned with fire; and their wives, and their sons, and their daughters, were taken captives.

modern.text: When David and his men came to the city, they found it burned down and their wives and sons and daughters taken captive.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א דָוִ֤ד וַֽאֲנָשָׁיו֙ אֶל הָעִ֔יר וְהִנֵּ֥ה שְׂרוּפָ֖ה בָּאֵ֑שׁ וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֛ם וּבְנֵיהֶ֥ם וּבְנֹתֵיהֶ֖ם נִשְׁבּֽוּ

verses.restored: David and people who were with him lifted their voice and wept until there was no strength in them to weep.

familiar.text: Then David and the people that were with him lifted up their voice and wept, until they had no more power to weep.

modern.text: So David and the troops with him lifted up their voices and wept until they had no strength left to weep.

original.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א דָוִ֜ד וְהָעָ֧ם אֲשֶׁר אִתּ֛וֹ אֶת קוֹלָ֖ם וַיִּבְכּ֑וּ עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֵין בָּהֶ֛ם כֹּ֖חַ לִבְכּֽוֹת

verses.restored: David's two wives were taken captive: Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

familiar.text: And David’s two wives were taken captives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

modern.text: David’s two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel, had been taken captive.

original.text: וּשְׁתֵּ֥י נְשֵֽׁי דָוִ֖ד נִשְׁבּ֑וּ אֲחִינֹ֨עַם֙ הַיִּזְרְעֵלִ֔ית וַאֲבִיגַ֕יִל אֵ֖שֶׁת נָבָ֥ל הַֽכַּרְמְלִֽי

verses.restored: David was greatly distressed, because people said to stone him, because soul of all people was bitter, each over his sons and over his daughters. But David strengthened himself in YHWH his Divine.

familiar.text: And David was greatly distressed; for the people spake of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters: but David encouraged himself in the LORD his God.

modern.text: And David was greatly distressed because the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of every man grieved for his sons and daughters. But David found strength in the LORD his God. David Destroys the Amalekites

original.text: וַתֵּ֨צֶר לְדָוִ֜ד מְאֹ֗ד כִּֽי אָמְר֤וּ הָעָם֙ לְסָקְל֔וֹ כִּֽי מָ֨רָה֙ נֶ֣פֶשׁ כָּל הָעָ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ עַל בנו וְעַל בְּנֹתָ֑יו וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֣ק דָּוִ֔ד בַּיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהָֽיו

verses.restored: David said to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, Please bring ephod near to me. Abiathar brought ephod near to David.

familiar.text: And David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech’s son, I pray thee, bring me hither the ephod. And Abiathar brought thither the ephod to David.

modern.text: Then David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, “Bring me the ephod.” So Abiathar brought it to him,

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד אֶל אֶבְיָתָ֤ר הַכֹּהֵן֙ בֶּן אֲחִימֶ֔לֶךְ הַגִּֽישָׁה נָּ֥א לִ֖י הָאֵפֹ֑ד וַיַּגֵּ֧שׁ אֶבְיָתָ֛ר אֶת הָאֵפֹ֖ד אֶל דָּוִֽד

verses.restored: David inquired of YHWH, saying, Shall I pursue after this band? Shall I overtake it? YHWH said to him, Pursue, because overtaking you shall overtake, and rescuing you shall rescue.

familiar.text: And David enquired at the LORD, saying, Shall I pursue after this troop? shall I overtake them? And he answered him, Pursue: for thou shalt surely overtake them, and without fail recover all.

modern.text: and David inquired of the LORD: “Should I pursue these raiders? Will I overtake them?” “Pursue them,” the LORD replied, “for you will surely overtake them and rescue the captives.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֨ל דָּוִ֤ד בַּֽיהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אֶרְדֹּ֛ף אַחֲרֵ֥י הַגְּדוּד הַזֶּ֖ה הַֽאַשִּׂגֶ֑נּוּ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ רְדֹ֔ף כִּֽי הַשֵּׂ֥ג תַּשִּׂ֖יג וְהַצֵּ֥ל תַּצִּֽיל

verses.restored: David went, he and six hundred men who were with him, and they came to wadi Besor, where those left behind remained.

familiar.text: So David went, he and the six hundred men that were with him, and came to the brook Besor, where those that were left behind stayed.

modern.text: So David and his six hundred men went to the Brook of Besor, where some stayed behind

original.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד ה֚וּא וְשֵׁשׁ מֵא֥וֹת אִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד נַ֣חַל הַבְּשׂ֑וֹר וְהַנּֽוֹתָרִ֖ים עָמָֽדוּ

verses.restored: David pursued, he and four hundred men, and two hundred men remained, who were too exhausted to cross wadi Besor.

familiar.text: But David pursued, he and four hundred men: for two hundred abode behind, which were so faint that they could not go over the brook Besor.

modern.text: because two hundred men were too exhausted to cross the brook. But David and four hundred men continued in pursuit.

original.text: וַיִּרְדֹּ֣ף דָּוִ֔ד ה֖וּא וְאַרְבַּע מֵא֣וֹת אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ מָאתַ֣יִם אִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּגְּר֔וּ מֵעֲבֹ֖ר אֶת נַ֥חַל הַבְּשֽׂוֹר

verses.restored: They found an Egyptian man in field and took him to David. They gave him bread and he ate, and they gave him water to drink.

familiar.text: And they found an Egyptian in the field, and brought him to David, and gave him bread, and he did eat; and they made him drink water;

modern.text: Now his men found an Egyptian in the field and brought him to David. They gave the man water to drink and food to eat—

original.text: וַֽיִּמְצְא֤וּ אִישׁ מִצְרִי֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וַיִּקְח֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ אֶל דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּתְּנוּ ל֥וֹ לֶ֨חֶם֙ וַיֹּ֔אכַל וַיַּשְׁקֻ֖הוּ מָֽיִם

verses.restored: They gave him a slice of cake of figs and two clusters/cakes of raisins. He ate, and his spirit returned to him, because he had not eaten bread and had not drunk water three days and three nights.

familiar.text: And they gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins: and when he had eaten, his spirit came again to him: for he had eaten no bread, nor drunk any water, three days and three nights.

modern.text: a piece of a fig cake and two clusters of raisins. So he ate and was revived, for he had not had any food or water for three days and three nights.

original.text: וַיִּתְּנוּ לוֹ֩ פֶ֨לַח דְּבֵלָ֜ה וּשְׁנֵ֤י צִמֻּקִים֙ וַיֹּ֔אכַל וַתָּ֥שָׁב רוּח֖וֹ אֵלָ֑יו כִּ֠י לֹֽא אָ֤כַל לֶ֨חֶם֙ וְלֹא שָׁ֣תָה מַ֔יִם שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יָמִ֖ים וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה לֵילֽוֹת

verses.restored: David said to him, To whom do you belong, and from where are you? He said, I am an Egyptian young man, servant of an Amalekite man. My master abandoned me because I became sick three days ago.

familiar.text: And David said unto him, To whom belongest thou? and whence art thou? And he said, I am a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite; and my master left me, because three days agone I fell sick.

modern.text: Then David asked him, “To whom do you belong, and where are you from?” “I am an Egyptian,” he replied, “the slave of an Amalekite. My master abandoned me three days ago when I fell ill.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֤וֹ דָוִד֙ לְֽמִי אַ֔תָּה וְאֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה אָ֑תָּה וַיֹּ֜אמֶר נַ֧עַר מִצְרִ֣י אָנֹ֗כִי עֶ֚בֶד לְאִ֣ישׁ עֲמָֽלֵקִ֔י וַיַּעַזְבֵ֧נִי אֲדֹנִ֛י כִּ֥י חָלִ֖יתִי הַיּ֥וֹם שְׁלֹשָֽׁה

verses.restored: We raided Negev of Cherethites, what belongs to Judah, and Negev of Caleb, and Ziklag we burned with fire.

familiar.text: We made an invasion upon the south of the Cherethites, and upon the coast which belongeth to Judah, and upon the south of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire.

modern.text: We raided the Negev of the Cherethites, the territory of Judah, and the Negev of Caleb, and we burned down Ziklag.”

original.text: אֲנַ֡חְנוּ פָּשַׁ֜טְנוּ נֶ֧גֶב הַכְּרֵתִ֛י וְעַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִֽיהוּדָ֖ה וְעַל נֶ֣גֶב כָּלֵ֑ב וְאֶת צִקְלַ֖ג שָׂרַ֥פְנוּ בָאֵֽשׁ

verses.restored: David said to him, Will you bring me down to this band? He said, Swear to me by Divine that you will not put me to death and will not shut me into hand of my master, and I will bring you down to this band.

familiar.text: And David said to him, Canst thou bring me down to this company? And he said, Swear unto me by God, that thou wilt neither kill me, nor deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will bring thee down to this company.

modern.text: “Will you lead me to these raiders?” David asked. And the man replied, “Swear to me by God that you will not kill me or deliver me into the hand of my master, and I will lead you to them.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ דָּוִ֔ד הֲתוֹרִדֵ֖נִי אֶל הַגְּד֣וּד הַזֶּ֑ה וַיֹּ֡אמֶר הִשָּׁבְעָה֩ לִּ֨י בֵֽאלֹהִ֜ים אִם תְּמִיתֵ֗נִי וְאִם תַּסְגִּרֵ֨נִי֙ בְּיַד אֲדֹנִ֔י וְאוֹרִֽדְךָ֖ אֶל הַגְּד֥וּד הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: He brought him down, and look, they were spread upon face of all land, eating and drinking and celebrating over all great spoil they had taken from land of Philistines and from land of Judah.

familiar.text: And when he had brought him down, behold, they were spread abroad upon all the earth, eating and drinking, and dancing, because of all the great spoil that they had taken out of the land of the Philistines, and out of the land of Judah.

modern.text: So he led David down, and there were the Amalekites spread out over all the land, eating, drinking, and celebrating the great amount of plunder they had taken from the land of the Philistines and the land of Judah.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣רִדֵ֔הוּ וְהִנֵּ֥ה נְטֻשִׁ֖ים עַל פְּנֵ֣י כָל הָאָ֑רֶץ אֹכְלִ֤ים וְשֹׁתִים֙ וְחֹ֣גְגִ֔ים בְּכֹל֙ הַשָּׁלָ֣ל הַגָּד֔וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָקְח֛וּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים וּמֵאֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: David struck them from twilight until evening of next day. Not a man of them escaped except four hundred young men who rode upon camels and fled.

familiar.text: And David smote them from the twilight even unto the evening of the next day: and there escaped not a man of them, save four hundred young men, which rode upon camels, and fled.

modern.text: And David struck them down from twilight until the evening of the next day. Not a man escaped, except four hundred young men who fled, riding off on camels.

original.text: וַיַּכֵּ֥ם דָּוִ֛ד מֵהַנֶּ֥שֶׁף וְעַד הָעֶ֖רֶב לְמָֽחֳרָתָ֑ם וְלֹֽא נִמְלַ֤ט מֵהֶם֙ אִ֔ישׁ כִּי֩ אִם אַרְבַּ֨ע מֵא֧וֹת אִֽישׁ נַ֛עַר אֲשֶׁר רָכְב֥וּ עַל הַגְּמַלִּ֖ים וַיָּנֻֽסוּ

verses.restored: David rescued all that Amalekites had taken, and David rescued his two wives.

familiar.text: And David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away: and David rescued his two wives.

modern.text: So David recovered everything the Amalekites had taken, including his two wives.

original.text: וַיַּצֵּ֣ל דָּוִ֔ד אֵ֛ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָקְח֖וּ עֲמָלֵ֑ק וְאֶת שְׁתֵּ֥י נָשָׁ֖יו הִצִּ֥יל דָּוִֽד

verses.restored: Nothing of theirs was missing, from small even to great, even sons and daughters, and from spoil even to all that they had taken for themselves. David returned all.

familiar.text: And there was nothing lacking to them, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, neither spoil, nor any thing that they had taken to them: David recovered all.

modern.text: Nothing was missing, young or old, son or daughter, or any of the plunder the Amalekites had taken. David brought everything back.

original.text: וְלֹ֣א נֶעְדַּר לָ֠הֶם מִן הַקָּטֹ֨ן וְעַד הַגָּד֜וֹל וְעַד בָּנִ֤ים וּבָנוֹת֙ וּמִשָּׁלָ֔ל וְעַ֛ד כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָקְח֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם הַכֹּ֖ל הֵשִׁ֥יב דָּוִֽד

verses.restored: David took all flock and herd. They drove them before that livestock and said, This is David's spoil.

familiar.text: And David took all the flocks and the herds, which they drave before those other cattle, and said, This is David’s spoil.

modern.text: And he recovered all the flocks and herds, which his men drove ahead of the other livestock, calling out, “This is David’s plunder!” The Spoils Are Divided

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח דָּוִ֔ד אֶת כָּל הַצֹּ֖אן וְהַבָּקָ֑ר נָהֲג֗וּ לִפְנֵי֙ הַמִּקְנֶ֣ה הַה֔וּא וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ זֶ֖ה שְׁלַ֥ל דָּוִֽד

verses.restored: David came to two hundred men who had been too exhausted to walk after David, whom they had made remain at wadi Besor. They went out to meet David and to meet people who were with him. David approached people and asked concerning their peace.

familiar.text: And David came to the two hundred men, which were so faint that they could not follow David, whom they had made also to abide at the brook Besor: and they went forth to meet David, and to meet the people that were with him: and when David came near to the people, he saluted them.

modern.text: When David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow him from the Brook of Besor, they came out to meet him and the troops with him. As David approached the men, he greeted them,

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֣א דָוִ֗ד אֶל מָאתַ֨יִם הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים אֲשֶֽׁר פִּגְּר֣וּ מִלֶּ֣כֶת אַחֲרֵ֣י דָוִ֗ד וַיֹּֽשִׁיבֻם֙ בְּנַ֣חַל הַבְּשׂ֔וֹר וַיֵּֽצְאוּ֙ לִקְרַ֣את דָּוִ֔ד וְלִקְרַ֖את הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר אִתּ֑וֹ וַיִּגַּ֤שׁ דָּוִד֙ אֶת הָעָ֔ם וַיִּשְׁאַ֥ל לָהֶ֖ם לְשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: Every evil and worthless man among men who had gone with David answered and said, Because they did not go with us, we will not give them from spoil that we rescued, except each man's wife and children, and let them lead them away and go.

familiar.text: Then answered all the wicked men and men of Belial, of those that went with David, and said, Because they went not with us, we will not give them ought of the spoil that we have recovered, save to every man his wife and his children, that they may lead them away, and depart.

modern.text: but all the wicked and worthless men among those who had gone with David said, “Because they did not go with us, we will not share with them the plunder we recovered, except for each man’s wife and children. They may take them and go.”

original.text: וַיַּ֜עַן כָּל אִֽישׁ רָ֣ע וּבְלִיַּ֗עַל מֵֽהָאֲנָשִׁים֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלְכ֣וּ עִם דָּוִד֒ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא הָלְכ֣וּ עִמִּ֔י לֹֽא נִתֵּ֣ן לָהֶ֔ם מֵהַשָּׁלָ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִצַּ֑לְנוּ כִּֽי אִם אִ֤ישׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ֙ וְאֶת בָּנָ֔יו וְיִנְהֲג֖וּ וְיֵלֵֽכוּ

verses.restored: David said, You shall not do so, my brothers, with what YHWH has given us. YHWH guarded us and gave into our hand band that came against us.

familiar.text: Then said David, Ye shall not do so, my brethren, with that which the LORD hath given us, who hath preserved us, and delivered the company that came against us into our hand.

modern.text: But David said, “My brothers, you must not do this with what the LORD has given us. He has protected us and delivered into our hands the raiders who came against us.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד לֹֽא תַעֲשׂ֥וּ כֵ֖ן אֶחָ֑י אֵ֠ת אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה לָ֨נוּ֙ וַיִּשְׁמֹ֣ר אֹתָ֔נוּ וַיִּתֵּ֗ן אֶֽת הַגְּד֛וּד הַבָּ֥א עָלֵ֖ינוּ בְּיָדֵֽנוּ

verses.restored: Who will listen to you concerning this matter? For as portion of one who goes down into battle, so portion of one who stays by baggage; together they shall divide.

familiar.text: For who will hearken unto you in this matter? but as his part is that goeth down to the battle, so shall his part be that tarrieth by the stuff: they shall part alike.

modern.text: Who will listen to your proposal? The share of the one who went to battle will match the share of the one who stayed with the supplies. They will share alike.”

familiar.text: And it was so from that day forward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel unto this day.

modern.text: And so it has been from that day forward. David established this statute as an ordinance for Israel to this very day.

modern.text: When David arrived in Ziklag, he sent some of the plunder to his friends, the elders of Judah, saying, “Here is a gift for you from the plunder of the LORD’s enemies.”

translation_notes: The women and children are captives and survivors, not property or 'spoil.' Recovery does not erase trauma or establish that all abductees were unharmed.
Collective weeping is presented without shame. Grief, exhaustion, anger, and loss of strength are embodied human responses.
The threat to stone David shows how traumatized communities can redirect rage inward. Distress explains but does not justify mob killing.

The Egyptian servant is abandoned when ill, deprived of food and water, and vulnerable to both armies. David's group feeds him before interrogation, and he negotiates explicit safety conditions before assisting.
His designation as Egyptian and servant/slave must not support xenophobia or slavery apologetics. He is a crucial agent with intelligence, memory, and bargaining power.
The battle remains lethal and prolonged. Rescue of captives does not make every act of violence, spoil-taking, or later political distribution ethically clean.
The two hundred are too exhausted to continue. David's equal-share rule rejects ableism, productivity hierarchy, and contempt for logistical or caregiving labor.
Returning wives and children is not a sufficient 'share'; people are not compensation. The disputed material goods are divided equally.
David's gifts to Judah also build political relationships and should not be spiritualized away from patronage and succession strategy.
safety_note: Center the captives, the abandoned Egyptian worker, the exhausted two hundred, and the grieving community. Do not treat people as spoil, shame trauma or fatigue, justify slavery, or glorify the retaliatory battle. The chapter's clearest constructive ethic is food before extraction, negotiated safety, full recovery, and equal sharing across different forms of labor.
